title: Field with its own contract: seen factor, second-order terms, fall and clock

key_results.statement: Exact, whole class: the compression $\hat C$ of $C$ onto $\varphi_0$ has a body part in the class $\mathcal C$ with $m_x=mN(x)$, $\eta_x=N(x)$, $\zeta_x=1$, $V_x=e_0$; it is the contract of an admissible description of $b$ and $c$.
Under (2.20): $N(x)\to N(x)+a_x$, $e_0\to e_0+c$, while $\varphi_0$, $\tilde\Phi_x$, $S$, $\varepsilon_x$, $\Delta_f$, $\nu$ and $\hat C$ are unchanged; $N(x)$ alone is not well defined.
Bound in R0, all $\lambda\ge0$: $\lVert Q_0\Psi(\lambda)\rVert\le\varepsilon M_{\max}\lambda$.
In R1, all $\lambda\ge0$ (order estimate of the constant): $\lVert Q_0\Psi(\lambda)\rVert\le2\epsilon_1[1+O(\epsilon_1^2+\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)]$.

Statistics of every schedule on $b$, $c$ are those of a sharp field with profile $N(x)$ up to $2\varepsilon M_{\max}\lambda_k$ (R0, bound) and up to $O(\epsilon_1^2)+O(\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f\lambda_k)$ (R1, order estimate): no term linear in $\epsilon_1$, range $\lambda\ll1/(\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f)$.
Sylvester equation for the block-off-diagonal generator and $H_{\rm eff}=\hat C-\tfrac12(\mathcal S_1^{\dagger}W_1+W_1^{\dagger}\mathcal S_1)+O(\epsilon_1^4\Delta_f)$ in R1.

Second-order term at leading order in $\epsilon_2$, $\epsilon_3$: $H^{(2)}=-\sum_x\gamma_xP_x\otimes\mathbb 1_2\otimes(m\mathbb 1_N+D)^2$ with $\gamma_x=\langle\tilde\Phi_xS\tilde\Phi_x\rangle$, $\lvert\gamma_x\rvert\le\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_f$.

First corrections: $H^{(2,1)}$ (factor $1-M_k^2c_x$ on the hopping, relative order $\epsilon_2$) and $H^{(3)}=\sum_x\gamma^{(3)}_xP_x\otimes\sigma_3\otimes\mathcal M^3$ (relative order $\epsilon_3$); remainder $O(\epsilon_1^2(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)^2\Delta_f)+O(\epsilon_1^4\Delta_f)$, with the ranges of $\lambda$.

Level blocks of the body part of $H_{\rm eff}$: on-site $(N(x)M_k+\gamma^{(3)}_xM_k^3)\sigma_3+(e_0-\gamma_xM_k^2)\mathbb 1_2$, hopping $-\tfrac{i\tau}{2}(1-M_k^2c_x)\sigma_1$; a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ at leading order for every member of $\mathcal D$.

With the first corrections the body part is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ up to the hopping phase if and only if (P): $\mu_{x,k}=N(x)M_k+\gamma^{(3)}_xM_k^3>0$ for all $x$, $k$, with the margin (P') against the remainder; sufficient: $\varepsilon\epsilon_1\epsilon_3<\min_xN(x)$; R1 does not imply (P).

Level data for $\Phi_x=N_0+xY$ at first order in $Y$: $\tau_k=\tau(1-2\rho_0M_k^2)$, $\hat M_k=M_k(1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2)$, $G_k=gM_k+\gamma^{(3)}_1M_k^3$, $\mathcal F_k=\gamma_1M_k^2$, $g_{\zeta,k}=-4M_k^2\operatorname{Re}\rho_Y$, $V_k=e_0-\gamma_0M_k^2$.

Inequalities of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ for the linear profiles with the first corrections: $\hat M_k>\lvert G_k\rvert L$ and $\lvert g_{\zeta,k}\rvert(L-\tfrac12)<1$ for all $k$, with two margins; R1 does not imply them.

For $\langle X\rangle=0$: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+\beta M_k^2]$ with $\beta=g(4\rho_0+\gamma^{(3)}_0)-\gamma^{(3)}_1$; the term in $\gamma_1$ is exact at leading order in $\epsilon_2$, $\epsilon_3$ and not small against $g$ in R1; the term in $\beta$ holds under (10.28).

Before the expansion, for $\langle X\rangle=0$ under (10.28): $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2\frac{(1-2\rho_0M_k^2)^2}{1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2}[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k-\gamma^{(3)}_1M_k^2]$; the term in $\beta$ of (10.13) exceeds the dropped terms only if $\lvert\gamma_1\rvert M_k(\epsilon_1^2+\lvert\gamma^{(3)}_0\rvert M_k^2)\ll\lvert\beta\rvert M_k^2$, in particular for $\gamma_1=0$.

For $\langle X\rangle=0$: at leading order in $\epsilon_2$, $\epsilon_3$ the fall from rest is level-independent (either branch, or both with the value $-\tau^2g$) if and only if $\gamma_1=0$; for the expression (10.13) with the first corrections, under (10.28), if and only if $\gamma_1=0$ and $\beta=0$ for $N\ge3$, with separate branch conditions for $N=2$.

For every $\langle X\rangle$ the record term $a^{\rm rec}_{k,\sigma}=-\sigma\frac{\tau_k^2}{\hat M_k}\kappa\langle X\rangle$ is added to (10.13); it is of zeroth order in $\epsilon_1$, odd in the branch and different for every two levels when $\langle X\rangle\neq0$.

For $\langle X\rangle\neq0$ the fall from rest is level-dependent in each branch for $N\ge3$ at leading order and for $N\ge4$ with the first corrections; exceptional members for $N=2$ and $N=3$; both branches with one value implies $\langle X\rangle=0$.

The uniform hopping phase $\theta_k=M_k^2\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y$ gives a branch start a velocity $v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)$ at first order in $Y$, bounded for all $\lambda$, which leaves the drift accelerations unchanged.

Branch start at rest, under (10.28): window-averaged velocity $\bar v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}=-\sigma\tau^2M_k\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y$, odd in the branch and different for every two levels; the sharp-label limit and the growth of $\lambda$ do not commute for the velocity itself.
Spacings $E^+_{x,k+1}-E^+_{x,k}=\frac{2\pi}{N\lambda_0}[N(x)-\gamma_x(M_k+M_{k+1})+\gamma^{(3)}_x(M_k^2+M_kM_{k+1}+M_{k+1}^2)]$, a polynomial identity; a spacing can vanish or be negative in R1.

The spacings are independent of $k$ at leading order if and only if $N=2$ or $\gamma_x=0$; with the first corrections if and only if $N=2$, or $N=3$ and $\gamma_x=3\gamma^{(3)}_xM_1$, or $N\ge4$ and $\gamma_x=\gamma^{(3)}_x=0$.

At leading order in $\epsilon_2$, $\epsilon_3$ the clock statistics of $S_{\rm clock}(x_0)$ is the ring-clock mixture (3.36) with the rate $\bar r(x_0)$ up to total variation $\tfrac12\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert d_{N-1}^2\lambda$; accuracy $\eta$ for $\lambda\le2\eta/(\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert d_{N-1}^2)$ when $N\ge3$, $\gamma_{x_0}\neq0$.

Ring clock with the one rate $r\in\mathbb R$; the mean rate $\lambda_0\bar r(x_0)=N(x_0)-\gamma_{x_0}\Sigma$ is positive, zero or negative in R1, (10.16) and (10.30) hold in each case, and for $r=0$ the clock stands and is no reference for a ratio of rates.

With the cubic term, wide start, under (10.28): mean rate $\bar r(x)=\lambda_0^{-1}[N(x)-\gamma_x\Sigma+\gamma^{(3)}_x(M_0^2+M_0M_{N-1}+M_{N-1}^2)]$ and accuracy $\eta$ for $\lambda\le2\eta/(\Xi_{x_0}d_{N-1}^2)$ when $N\ge3$, $\Xi_{x_0}\neq0$.

For $D_0=1-\gamma_0\Sigma\neq0$, leading order in $\epsilon_2$, $\epsilon_3$, every $\langle X\rangle$: relative gradient of the mean rate $(g-\gamma_1\Sigma)/D_0$ and defect of (4.24) $\mathcal R_k=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma/D_0)+g\gamma_0\Sigma/D_0-\kappa\langle X\rangle/M_k]$, exact in $\gamma_0\Sigma$; (4.24) holds for all levels if and only if $\gamma_1=0$, $g\gamma_0=0$, $\langle X\rangle=0$ ($N\ge3$), or $\gamma_0(g-\gamma_1\Sigma)=0$ and $\gamma_1M_0M_1=-\kappa\langle X\rangle$ ($N=2$).

The comparison of (4.24) is defined if and only if $D_0\neq0$, with the margin $\lvert D_0\rvert\gg\varepsilon\epsilon_1(\epsilon_3+\epsilon_1^2+\epsilon_2^2)$; hierarchy (H): $\lvert\gamma_0\rvert\Sigma\ll1$, sufficient $2\epsilon_1\varepsilon\ll1$; neither R1 nor (10.28) implies (H).

Under (H) of (10.35), for $\langle X\rangle=0$, leading order in $\epsilon_2$, $\epsilon_3$: $\mathcal R_k=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma)+g\gamma_0\Sigma]$ with $\Sigma=M_0+M_{N-1}$; it contains data of the body.

Under (H) of (10.35), for every $\langle X\rangle$: $\mathcal R_k=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma)+g\gamma_0\Sigma-\kappa\langle X\rangle/M_k]$; for $\langle X\rangle\neq0$ the relation (4.24) fails already for a sharp field.

Members with a vanishing mean rate, $D_0=0$, exist in R1 with the margins of (10.28): the relative gradient is not defined there, and the form of (4.24) multiplied by the comparison rate equals $\tau^2\bar r(1)$ and holds if and only if $g=\gamma_1\Sigma$.

Cells: $N(x)=n_x$, $\varepsilon=\max_x\varepsilon_x$, $\Delta_f=\min_x\Delta_x$, $\gamma_x=\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x$, $\rho_{xy}=\delta_{xy}\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x^2$, $\gamma^{(3)}_x=0$; the body part is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ with (P) for every cell description.

Exact on-site solution of a cell: eigenvalues $\pm M_kn_x-\Omega_{x,k}$ (lower) and $\pm M_kn_x+\Omega_{x,k}$ (upper) with $\Omega_{x,k}=\sqrt{\Delta_x^2/4+M_k^2\varepsilon_x^2}$; the overlap $\cos\tfrac{\alpha_{x,k}}2$ of the lower eigenvector with $\lvert0\rangle$ multiplies the hopping, in agreement with (10.18).

The subclass $\mathcal L$ of item 4(c): $n_x=1+gx$, $\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x=\gamma_0+\gamma_1x$ and $c_x=\rho_0+\rho_1(x+\tfrac12)$ for all $x$; cells with a constant $\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x=\gamma$ are in $\mathcal L$ if and only if $\gamma=0$ or $1/\Delta_x+1/\Delta_{x+1}$ is linear in $x$.

Cells of $\mathcal L$, $\langle X\rangle=0$: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+2g\rho_0M_k^2]$; for constant $\gamma$ the branch-odd term vanishes while the level offsets, the defect $\tau^2g\gamma\Sigma/(1-\gamma\Sigma)$ of (4.24) and the level-dependent hopping remain; for cells outside $\mathcal L$ the results of items 4(a), 4(b) hold and the fall is not stated.

Orders: nothing changes at order $\epsilon_1$; the first change is at order $\epsilon_1^2$, of relative size $\lvert\gamma_x\rvert M_{\max}\le\epsilon_1\varepsilon$, which is not a small number of R1; the velocity from the hopping phase appears at order $\epsilon_1^2$ and first order in $\epsilon_2$.

open_issues: (10.6), the R1 part of (10.7) and the remainders of (10.10) are order estimates: their constants and the dependence of (10.7) on the number of readings are not bounded explicitly.

The accelerations (10.13), (10.20), (10.22) and the velocity (10.24), (10.25) are those of the description with H_eff; for the description with C only the agreement of the statistics within (10.10) is derived.

Members in which (P) of (10.27) or (10.28) fails or holds without its margin: the statements with the first corrections are not derived; the exchange of the branch places is not worked out, and a rest term that changes sign along the chain is not treated.

Members whose comparison rate vanishes within the margin of (10.35): the sign of the mean rate is decided by terms not kept, and neither (10.34) nor (10.36) is derived for them; the margin itself is an order estimate.
With γ_1 ≠ 0 the term τ²βM_k² of (10.13) is larger than the terms dropped after (10.32) only under the hierarchy stated there; the terms of fourth order of H_eff, of the same size, are not computed.

Outside the scope of the question: the fall from rest, the defect of (4.24) and the clock range of cells with n_x = 1 + g x whose γ_x or c_x is not linear in x; they need a result for level profiles that are not linear (a later package).
(10.16) has the orders of (3.36) and the leading order in ε_2, ε_3; (10.30) holds in the wide-start limit only; the loss of clock coherence by the level-dependent force and velocity is not treated.
For profiles of the field that are not linear the hopping phase depends on x; its effect is given only as a change of the start, and the velocity (10.24), (10.25) is derived for the linear profiles.
Where 2ε_1 + 2ε_2 + ε_3 ≥ 1 only the R0 statements (10.1), (10.2), (10.4) and the first part of (10.7) are derived; whether an effective description exists there is not determined, except for ε = 0.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of all coefficients, accelerations, the velocity, the clock quantities, D_0 and both sides of (10.36)
Sharp field (ε = 0) and field operators commuting with C_f: all new terms vanish, (2.3) and (4.22) are reproduced, D_0 = 1

Exact on-site problems against the expansion: the cell, the two-place field with a negative rest term, and the two-level member with a vanishing mean rate; (10.34) reduces to (10.17), (10.26) for small γ_0 Σ
